_note: Physics parameters (spec 7.10). 'values' is what the physics loads; 'docs' gives each value's unit, source and note. Change a value only with its source.

ball_mass_kg.source: Mathavan, Jackson & Parkin (2010), Proc. IMechE C 224(9):1863-1873, sec. 3.2: 'For a snooker ball, M = 0.1406 kg and R = 26.25 mm' (their measured snooker set); spec 6.1 starting value 0.141
ball_mass_kg.note: WPBSA rules fix only the diameter and a 3 g spread within a set. Retail listings for Aramith Tournament Champion 52.5 mm sets quote about 142 g (+-2 g), Aramith Premier 52.4 mm about 126-128 g; Mathavan's measured ball sits inside that spread and is the ball the cushion model was fitted with.

slide_friction.source: Mathavan, Jackson & Parkin (2009), 'Application of high-speed imaging to determine the dynamics of billiards', Am. J. Phys. 77(9):788-794, doi:10.1119/1.3157159: snooker ball on a Riley Renaissance table, sliding deceleration 1.75-2.40 m/s^2 (0.178-0.245); 0.212 is the average Mathavan et al. (2010) sec. 3.2 use, as cushion_table_friction does
slide_friction.note: Ball-cloth sliding friction. Sets how long stun and screw last before the ball grips. Was 0.2 (Alciatore's typical pool value, physical properties FAQ 0.15-0.4).

roll_friction.source: C11 lag (docs/calibration/targets.md) at the fast end of the snooker evidence: Mathavan et al. (2009) Am. J. Phys. 77(9):788-794 measured 0.0127-0.0129 on an unheated laboratory Riley Renaissance (10 x 5 ft); spec 7.10 0.005-0.01; Alciatore physical properties FAQ 0.005-0.015 (pool)
roll_friction.note: Rolling resistance. The only snooker measurement (0.0127) is slower than C11 allows (effective slope at most 0.0105, competition pool cloth); a tournament table's heated slate and freshly ironed cloth play faster than a lab table, so this takes the C11 range's slow end: the lag needs a 2.14 m/s cue ball (C11 band 1.55-2.32) and its last length takes 8.4 s (effective slope 0.0101). Was 0.008. Owner judges the pace by feel in M2.

spin_friction_per_r.source: pooltool (Apache-2.0) BallParams.u_sp_proportionality = 10*2/5/9; Alciatore physical properties FAQ: spin deceleration 5-15 rad/s^2
spin_friction_per_r.note: Spinning friction divided by R; side spin decays at 5/2 * this * g = 10.9 rad/s^2, mid-range of Alciatore's 5-15.

ball_restitution.source: spec 7.4; Alciatore physical properties FAQ: ball-ball 0.92-0.98
ball_restitution.note: Tuned against C2/C3 (stun stop and follow-through). Mathavan et al. (2009) Table I measured object-ball speeds 5-9% under the e = 1 theory, which hints at the low end; kept mid-range.

ball_friction_a.source: least-squares refit (spec 7.4) of TP A.14's model to the published half-ball-region stun throw: Alciatore, 'Throw - Part II: results', Billiards Digest Sept 2006, Diagram 4 (25, 30, 35 deg at 1, 3, 7 mph) and Jewett 1995 (27, 30, 36 deg); fixture core/tests/fixtures/reference/throw_published.json
ball_friction_a.note: Ball-ball friction mu = a + b exp(-c v_rel), v_rel the contact sliding speed in m/s; gives throw and spin transfer (C6). TP A.14's own fit (a 0.009951, b 0.108, c 1.088, from Marlow's data) threw 4.86 / 3.55 / 1.70 deg at a half-ball stun hit at 1 / 3 / 7 mph against 4.5 / 4.1 / 3.45 measured (RMS 1.23 deg over 17 points); the refit gives 4.86 / 4.16 / 3.39 (RMS 0.22 deg against Alciatore's 9 points, 0.55 over all 17; 1 mph is capped by the balls gearing, 4.86 deg). mu runs 0.13 at 0.1 m/s to 0.058 above 2 m/s, inside Alciatore's published 0.03-0.08 at playing speeds. No snooker-ball throw data was found; these are pool balls, the same phenolic resin.

ball_rest_speed_m_s.source: M1 simulator finding: inelastic collapse in break-off packs
ball_rest_speed_m_s.note: Slower ball-ball approaches resolve as a sustained push (both roll on together); invisible at 1 mm/s.

cushion_restitution.source: Mathavan, Jackson & Parkin (2010), Proc. IMechE C 224(9):1863-1873, sec. 3.5: e_e = 0.98 with mu_w = 0.14 minimise the RMS error against measured snooker rebounds
cushion_restitution.note: e_e in the Mathavan model; with the friction terms it gives the speed-dependent loss (C7). A rolling ball straight in rebounds at 0.911 of its speed, matching the 0.910 low-speed gradient Mathavan et al. (2009) Am. J. Phys. 77:788 measured (their 0.818 is a straight-line fit over 0.28-3.5 m/s that includes the high-speed fall-off).

cushion_friction.source: Mathavan, Jackson & Parkin (2010), Proc. IMechE C 224(9):1863-1873, sec. 3.5: mu_w = 0.14 (fitted with e_e = 0.98)

cushion_table_friction.source: Mathavan, Jackson & Parkin (2010), Proc. IMechE C 224(9):1863-1873, sec. 3.2: mu_s = 0.212, the average of their measured 0.178-0.245 (Am. J. Phys. 77:788, 2009)
cushion_table_friction.note: Ball-cloth friction during the cushion impact; equal to slide_friction.

cushion_contact_height_m.source: Mathavan, Jackson & Parkin (2010), Proc. IMechE C 224(9):1863-1873: h = 7R/5 (sin theta = 2/5)
cushion_contact_height_m.note: Sets theta = asin((h - R) / R), the angle of the cushion's push; running and check side depend on it (C8).

cushion_rigid_limit_m_s.source: Mathavan, Jackson & Parkin (2010), Proc. IMechE C 224(9):1863-1873, Fig. 7: the model holds up to 2.5 m/s normal speed
cushion_rigid_limit_m_s.note: Above it the cushion stops acting rigid; restitution falls by cushion_restitution_slope_per_m_s.

cushion_restitution_slope_per_m_s.source: Mathavan, Jackson & Parkin (2010), Proc. IMechE C 224(9):1863-1873, Fig. 7(b): least-squares fit to the measured rebounds above 2.5 m/s (RMS error 0.219 -> 0.068 m/s)
cushion_restitution_slope_per_m_s.note: Firm cushion and jaw hits lose more than the rigid model says.

cushion_restitution_min.source: Alciatore TP B.6 typical rail restitution 0.7 (range 0.6-0.9); Mathavan et al. 2009 (Am. J. Phys. 77:788) measured rebound curve carried to 5 m/s (0.673)
cushion_restitution_min.note: Floor for cushion and jaw restitution on hard hits, reached at 4.25 m/s normal speed; no measurements exist beyond ~3.5 m/s.

jaw_restitution.source: documented starting value, no published measurement found for snooker jaws (the jaw rubber alone would suggest 0.98); spec 6.3 owner check
jaw_restitution.note: Jaws use the cushion model with their own restitution: firm balls rattle, slow ones drop. The owner tunes it by feel in M2.

cue_mass_kg.note: Effective cue mass in the tip impulse.

cue_tip_restitution.source: Alciatore, billiards.colostate.edu physical properties: leather tips 0.71-0.75 (top of the range)

cue_end_mass_kg.source: pooltool (Apache-2.0) SNOOKER_GENERIC cue end mass (ball mass / 30); stick_ball/squirt.py model
cue_end_mass_kg.note: Squirt grows with this: 2.0 degrees at maximum side (C9 asks 1-3).

miscue_speed_factor.note: A miscued ball keeps at most this fraction of the full-hit speed.

miscue_max_angle_rad.note: A miscue sends the ball within this angle of the aim.

cue_clearance_m.note: Margin the cue keeps over a rail or ball when the elevation is raised.

max_cue_speed_m_s.source: starting guess: above the hardest snooker shots

nap_tick_ratio.note: A rolling ball's nap is re-evaluated each time its speed falls by this factor.

nap_lateral_coeff.source: starting guess: about 1-2 cm of drift over a slow 1 m roll
nap_lateral_coeff.note: Spec 7.8: the owner's feel decides it.

nap_spin_coeff.note: Side spin holding with the nap; spec 7.8.

nap_speed_ref_m_s.note: Speed at which the lateral term equals nap_lateral_coeff * g.

time_cap_s.note: A shot still moving after this is stopped and logged (C12).

zero_time_s.note: Events closer than this are simultaneous.

max_zero_time_chain.note: Simultaneous events in a row before the guard trips (spec 7.7).
